heroHeadline: Russia Strikes Ukraine with 73 Missiles (8 Zircon) + 656 Drones — Kyiv Residential Building Collapses; 17+ Killed; Zelensky Sends Urgent Patriot Letter to Trump
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,559 (June 2, 2026), Russia launched one of the largest combined missile and drone barrages of the war overnight — 73 missiles including 8 Zircon hypersonics (the largest single-use of that weapon in the conflict) plus 656 Shahed-type attack drones. Ukraine's air defenses intercepted 40 missiles and 602 drones, but a 9-story residential building in Kyiv's Podilskyi district was partially collapsed with people feared trapped; 6 people were killed and 63–65 wounded in the capital. Dnipro sustained 4+ killed and 16 wounded; Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Poltava, Khmelnytskyi and Sumy regions were also struck — bringing the national toll to at least 17–18 killed and 100+ wounded. President Zelensky responded with an urgent public appeal to the United States and a formal letter to both the White House and Congress: 'Assistance from the United States in supplying missiles for Patriot systems is absolutely necessary.' Simultaneously, Ukraine struck Russia's Ilsky oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai for at least the 16th time, destroyed a Pantsir-S1 air defense system, and hit a Russian vessel in occupied Crimea. On the frontline, 178 combat engagements were recorded; Pokrovsk repelled 36 Russian assault attempts. Russian cumulative losses reached approximately 1,366,910 personnel, with 1,440 eliminated in the preceding 24 hours.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, ABC News, NPR, CNN, CBS News, Times of Israel, Time, PBS NewsHour, RBC Ukraine, Militarnyi, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
